dimensions.assessment: Involves federal regulators, GAO researchers, telecommunications providers, 911/988 system operators, and crisis centers.
dimensions.evidence: telecommunications service providers, 911 system service providers, public safety answering points, and local crisis centers

dimensions.assessment: Effects are primarily administrative, consisting of notices of inquiry, studies, and reports to congressional committees without mandating new rules or funding.
dimensions.evidence: instruct the Federal Communications Commission to initiate a notice of inquiry and instruct the Government Accountability Office to complete a study and report

dimensions.assessment: The source does not specify direct federal appropriations or economic impacts, though it requires assessing potential costs and funding requirements.
Requires specific investigative and reporting actions by federal agencies but does not amend substantive telecommunications mandates or create permanent regulatory programs.
dimensions.evidence: Federal Communications Commission shall initiate a notice of inquiry

dimensions.assessment: Involves one-time deadlines of 180 and 270 days for reports and inquiries.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 270 days after the date of enactment of this Act

importance_detail.rationale: S. 3199 directs the Federal Communications Commission and the Government Accountability Office to conduct studies, inquiries, and reports regarding challenges to transmitting geolocation data with 988 calls.
